rv.q: When it’s good, “Kinky Boots,” the new Broadway musical with the rocking Cyndi Lauper score, is sweetly, vivaciously, irresistibly good. And when it’s not so good — well, let’s not dwell for the moment on the not-so-good. The show is the sort of party for which you will be more than pleased to find yourself on the guest list.
Much crucial work has been done since the Chicago tryout, successful as it was.
The overall effect is nigh irresistible; if you’ve been low about this season’s musicals, Kinky Boots may be just the thing to get you back on your feet.
Lauper's at ease on Broadway in the likable but heavy-handed show.

The fact that her infectious spirit shines through every number in her first Broadway musical score is unquestionably the chief asset of Kinky Boots, helping to elevate the show above its familiar template.
What makes 'Kinky Boots' work is that Mr. Lauper and Mr. Mitchell have managed to wed their up-tempo, heartstring-tugging material to a story that is genuinely moving without being maudlin.
Cyndi Lauper's score has the driving energy and uplifting spirit of a roller derby, and unless they get hung up on the show's existential message, auds are likely to love it to death.
The spirit of these scenes is unassailable; the goopiness that they add to the last half-hour of the show isn't.
The production would be unthinkable without Porter.
Filling the niche with cheer and fine craftsmanship now is 'Kinky Boots.'
That sincerity comes through in “Kinky Boots.”
For a musical with such racy themes, it would be difficult to picture a more conservative, family-friendly show.
If “Kinky Boots” weren’t such a cheesy commercial mess, it might actually be fun.
Indeed, this high-energy spectacle with a heart is musical comedy at its finest.
Kinky Boots has similarly been resuscitated and revitalized into a terrifically entertaining musical with plenty of heart as well as with a plethora of heels by its collaborators.
Thanks to Porter's star-making turn, Kinky Boots delivers some pumps-up kicks.
Even with some stumbles, “Kinky Boots” is a high time.

"There’s no use putting up a fight with “Kinky Boots.” This is the feel-good musical of the season. Yes, Harvey Fierstein’s funny book is a bit too bald, Cyndi Lauper’s catchy songs are more lyrically repetitive than they should be, and director-choreographer Jerry Mitchell slights character and story in favor of splashy production numbers.
This cast refuses to let you go until you are smothered in a good time.
What the duo has conjured together in 'Kinky Boots' is a vibrant, if choppy tale about carving your own identity, with bold, brassy music that delivers on its promise.
By the end, the talented Porter has veritably become Whitney Houston while learning the importance of being a man.
It's that quality that makes Kinky Boots rise above the cliches that threaten to trip it up.
Kinky Boots is a show that knows exactly what it wants to be and how to get there, even if the path it takes is more conventional than its subject matter might suggest.
It’s sort of a cross between La Cage Aux Folles and Billy Elliot with a bit of Sister Act and The Full Monty thrown in for good measure.
“Kinky Boots” is professionally put together, it’s entertaining…and it’s both safe and familiar.
What "Kinky Boots" sorely lacks is a dramatic commitment to what it's doing.

With Mr. Porter, as Lola, and Stark Sands, as Charlie, back on stage together for a limited run through January, “Kinky Boots” feels like Broadway’s hottest new musical, rather than one five years into its run.
Kinky Boots, a winning musical to celebrate and applaud.
Kinky Boots is a feel-good musical that succeeds in being both entertaining and emotionally resonant.
Kinky Boots and its cast get a standing ovation because they have earned and deserve it.

cn.t: Critics find "Kinky Boots" a feel-good crowd-pleaser with an infectious Cyndi Lauper score and Billy Porter's charismatic performance, though some fault its overly safe, predictable approach to its drag queen premise.
